key: With offerings I propitiate the branches of this swift-moving God, the bounteous Visnu.
s: In a hymn where the assembly gathers to praise the gods and asks them for riches, the singer turns to Visnu; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 7.40.5, takes Visnu as comprising all the gods, citing a Vedic text, and the other gods as though his branches.

evidence.gloss: At the offering, with oblations, food in the form of oblations, of this god Viṣṇu, who is to be reached, the showerer of desires, who comprises all the gods (sarvadevātmaka), according to the Vedic text ‘Viṣṇu is all the deities’ (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1.1, the editor’s reference): the other gods are vayāḥ, as it were branches.

reason: Second judgement: the refuter is right on the plain sense and the entry can be put right. Re-ran verse.js (ok, Rig Veda 7.40.5 at [555,5], 13 words, no dash) and packet.js --verse 7.40.5 and 7.40.1. Sāyaṇa's words on 7.40.5 are there verbatim: viṣṇoḥ sarvadevātmakasya, the śruti 'viṣṇuḥ sarvā devatāḥ', anye devāḥ vayāḥ śākhā iva bhavanti; Wilson's note and Griffith's note on 5 (quoting Wilson, 'a text cited by the scholiast') confirm it is his. The reading 'comprising all the gods, citing a Vedic text, and the other gods as though his branches' stands. CHANGED the context clause only: 'a hymn calling the gods to the rite' imported Sāyaṇa's address to the gods in his gloss on 7.40.1; in Griffith 7.40.1 the audience of the synod gathers to begin the praise of the swift gods (Griffith's note: praise of the Gods), and vv. 2 to 4 and 6 ask named gods for riches and protection. Now 'In a hymn where the assembly gathers to praise the gods and asks them for riches'. Entry-check ok on the corrected entry (scratch/RV-d070-p.json).
